utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May we begin in the usual manner by taking today's appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honours, Alexis Demirdjian, assisted by Case Manager Crispian Smith; and Senior Trial Attorney, Thomas Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic; Slobodan Cvijetic; Ms. Deirdre Montgomery; and Ms. Tatjana Savic, who is presently outside of the courtroom, appearing for Stanisic Defence team this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We have been alerted that there may be one or two preliminary matters before the witness is brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is in relation to the next witness, not this one, ST-216, if you recall we sought to add him to the list in December. And At that time we proposed to call him either as 92 ter or as a viva voce. And as 92 ter, if you remember, we proposed to call him for two hours. You requested clarification in February, we filed clarification saying that we would be only saving one hour if we called him as 92 ter. So in the end, we still have to call him as a viva voce, which you did grant; however, you said it would be for two hours. Now having proofed the witness over the weekend and seeing the number of documents I have, I will try my best but I wish to be granted the extra hour for the time being, and if I don't use it, then we can erase that. But I think that considering that he has never testified before and that we need to establish the background, his role as the prison warden, the type of procedure that was present before we get to the conflict, I would I would need that extra probably half an hour, 45 minutes to establish that before getting to the crucial elements. For that reason, I would ask for an additional hour. One more matter that might be of significance is that at this time we haven't confirmed any other witness after this -- after the second witness today. We're still waiting to heat if we have another witness for Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do the Defence have any views on this application for the additional hour for this witness, number 216?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We do not oppose, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, the application is granted. Three hours for Witness ST-216.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I alerted the Trial Chamber that I have one preliminary matter that I would like the guidance from the Trial Chamber. And I will speak in Serbian very shortly. [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not know to which extent you are informed of this, but around the Easter holidays, or just after the Easter holidays, a Croatian website published the official register of Croatian defenders, that is participants in the war operations in Croatia from 1991 through 1995. To the extent I have been able to establish, that document is an official document of the Republic of Croatia. However, it was put up on the website, as I've also been able to determine -- been able to determine from media reporting by an unauthorised person. Based on my knowledge so as far, it's my impression that there is no question of authenticity. It's, rather, a question of authorisation and the security of Croatia and some other issues over the publication of this register of defenders. It's the website of www.registarbranitelja.com, and it includes information about affiliations to various units in the Army of Croatia, the place of residence. There is also a search engine; you can put in a name and you get information about the person concerned, their movement through the service, career, et cetera. Two or three months ago, as you may remember, Your Honours, we had a similar situation, when we were discussing whether documents from the public domain, such as the Internet, may be used. On that earlier occasion a different document was in question, and Ms. Korner was opposed to its use. The Trial Chamber was of the view that the public domain, as such, is acceptable, but that it would be decided whether such documents can be used on a case-to-case basis. I discussed this already with my colleagues from the Prosecution, namely, that I intend to raise this issue in a preliminary way, and to seek instructions from the Trial Chamber on how to proceed. The next witness who is about to be heard refers to certain persons of Croatian nationality as persons who had spent a certain time with him together in detention or in a collection centre, and based on the allegations made by this witness, some of these persons had been killed, and he has allegedly knowledge about it. In my searches, I arrived at quite different information or at least information that challenges such allegations made by this witness. I printed out those pages from the website. They have been uploaded into e-court, and, of course, there is no translation available because all this happened over the weekend and there was no possibility to translate anything. But only names and numbers are concerned, so I don't think there will be any need to seek an official translation, unless the Trial Chamber demands it. This is what I wanted to present to the Trial Chamber and to seek instructions, in which way it would be most appropriate for me to use these documents in my cross-examination of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, there are two things that I'm not clear on. The last -- what I understood you to have said is that there are only names and numbers concerned, and therefore the question of translating them doesn't arise. Did I understand that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Because when you -- when you enter the website, there are -- there are -- there's small places where with you can type in the name, the surname and the name, plus the additional option is that you -- you print down the name of the -- of the unit which you are looking for, the special --or special name of the unit that you're looking for. And once you click on a search, then the name and the surname of the person appears with the name of the unit where he participated and the time of his participation in that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So that partly answers the second question that I was going ask, which is, do I understand that this is a -- that this website is essentially a reference tool and the -- it is a means by which you would -- you could access information in respect of particular persons as would you wish to? In other words, it isn't a question of the entirety of the website being something that you would have wished to incorporate by whatever means. It is merely the -- the result of particular searches that you -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. Because it is basically a search engine which gives you the opportunity to access the database which contains this is data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution has concerns about these kind of documents. As Your Honours will know, these days almost anything can be posted on the Internet by anybody. I don't know much about this. I heard briefly from Mr. Zecevic before we started today, I think last weeks I heard something about it in a decision in the hallway in our office. There was a -- as I understand in Croatia there was a great controversial about this particular collection, that it was posted and then -- I had heard -- I don't know, maybe Mr. Zecevic can enlighten. And heard that it had been withdrawn or removed from the website. I don't know if that's correct. He is shaking his head no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just briefly. It has been remove for one day and then it has been reinstated. And it is still operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Be that as it may, my concern is, again, the provenance of the document, we know what the website purports to be, but we only know that because it says it itself. If these documents are genuine and authentic, I would suggest the Defence make a Request for Assistance through the usual channels. We get something from the ministry stamped and confirmed, et cetera. Now if all Mr. Zupljanin wants to do at this point is use it as a good faith basis for asking a question on cross-examination, I don't have a problem with that. For example, the witness says, I was in detention with somebody named Franjo Boban, or something, a Croat name. And Mr. Zecevic says, Well, are you aware that Franjo Boban was apparently still alive in 1994 and serving in the Croatian services? He can ask that question. But then he has to live with the answer from the defendant. At this point, I don't think he is entitled to introduce some page he printed out from his computer off the Internet to challenge a witness. He can ask him question if he got a good faith basis to ask the question. But I don't think we have enough information about the authenticity and the veracity of that document on the website. So that would be my suggestion to the Trial Chamber, at this stage, how to proceed with this evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We -- we thank counsel for their observations. Baring in -- and we are particularly concerned about the caution that Mr. Hannis has raised. But we -- we appreciate the value which this document may have to the Trial Chamber, so it is something that we will discuss ourselves and indicate to counsel our views after a break or -- or sometime certainly before the witness comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry is it -- Mr. Zecevic, is it present witness or the witness to follow that the -- your --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The present witness. The present witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] we have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the first break, I guess. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, could you have the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could you begin by telling the Tribunal your name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Edin Hadzovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And your date of birth is when, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 18 June 1951, in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your profession or occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I used to be a clerk, and now I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. You have testified previously before this Tribunal, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, having previously testified, you would be familiar with the procedure, but I would, nevertheless, remind you that the way in which testimony is elicited is that the side calling you - in this case, the Prosecution - would begin by asking you questions, and then the side opposite would have an opportunity to cross-examine you. The Prosecution could then re-examine, and the Judges or the Chamber may themselves have questions of you. You have been called under expedited procedure having regard to your previous testimony, and the time that the Prosecution would spend with you is not as long as it would have been on -- when you first gave evidence. And with that, I would invite the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The time - thanks. The time that the Prosecution has is an hour, and cross -- the counsel for the first accused, Mr. Stanisic, has two hours; and the other side has requested only a quarter of an hour. So with that, I would invite counsel for the Prosecution to begin their examination-in-chief. There is one other point that I would make. There is a pattern of sitting which the Tribunal follows, largely for technical reasons in terms of the tapes that have to be changed, and so we sit for no longer than an hour and a half at one stretch. In fact, it is shorter than that. But, of course, if there any point at which you are distressed by any reason and you need for the Chamber to take a break before the ordinary time of breaking would occur, please indicate that to us and we would accommodate you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hadzovic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, you met investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in March 2001 and provided a statement at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And yesterday, when we met, you were given a chance to review this statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And while I'm asking the question, if we could display 65 ter 10344. Mr. Hadzovic, in March 2001 when you provided that statement, you answered the questions to the best of your knowledge at that time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we will be dealing with your supplemental statements during the course of this testimony. But I believe you have made one correction to your ICTY statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could go to page 7, both in the English and the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, at paragraph 4 of the statement in your language, this is the first paragraph in the English version, the paragraph starts with: "Until the 18th of May, 1992 ..." Now is it correct that in a supplemental statement you corrected that date and you indicated that it was the 18th of June, not the 18th of May?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, since you provided this statement, you testified in the case against Predrag Kujundzic in the state court of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you testified in November 2009 in the case against Stanisic and Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, finally, two weeks ago you met with Investigator Michael Koehler and you provided a supplemental statement.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I wish to tender the 92 ter statement in evidence, and I will be dealing orally with the supplemental statement he provided two weeks ago as well as the corrections he made therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1296.1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, in your statement in 2001, you stated that you were arrested on the 8th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And for reference, this is page 5 of the B/C/S version and page 4 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now two weeks ago in your supplementary statement, you provided some slightly different data or clarification. Could you provide that clarification here, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: When Doboj was liberated, according to the Serbian side, as they put it, Doboj was raided. During the raid, all the Muslims and Croats or, rather, the Bosnians and Croats who stayed behind were arrested. And on the 3rd of May all of this was over, and we were brought back on the 6th of May. Then, on the 11th of May, there was a new raid. We were picked up. All the men who were found in their houses were picked up. My first -- next door neighbours came. They put us in a police van, in a windowless police van, and they took to us prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on the same page of that statement you stated that soldiers arrested you on the 8th of May. Could you specify what these soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage military uniforms and red berets. We understood that they had come from Banja Luka, that they were some sort of the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How did you conclude that they were from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: My next door neighbour was a native of Banja Luka. He was a Serb. They didn't take him. And they told him that they were coming from the same area as he hailed from, and they didn't take him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on that occasion, who else was arrested with you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: My next door neighbours, Faruk Ajanovic, Fehro Mujakovic, and another man who was picked up on the road to hospital. He put him to the police van as well, and we were all taken to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you mentioned in your statement that you were placed in this police van, and you just stated it again. Where were you taken first?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: We were first taken to the Doboj police premises, the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in the Doboj police premises, where exactly were you taken?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: We were taken behind the police building, where there's a garage. This is where the van came, and they unloaded us from the van. It's an enclosed police compound where their vehicles are parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when they unloaded you, where were you brought next?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Then they took us to the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was there any -- on any specific floor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: They took us through the back door on -- onto the ground floor where the duty policemen's offices are, and the gate booth, and probably some room for interrogation, and a waiting room, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now you mentioned in your statement that you waited quite a long time and that you were interviewed by a man by the name of Branislav Petricevic. Now which organisation did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was an inspector with the CSB, a police inspector. He is an economist by profession, and we used to attend the same grammar school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on that, occasion did you -- did he ask you to provide a statement?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In your statement on the same page you say that Petricevic told you your half brother by the name of Zulfo Ciric is already detained in cell number 7. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did your half brother work at the time? What was his profession at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: My brother has an a university degree in economics. He was the head for planning and development in Doboj, and after that, he was the CEO of Bosnaprevoz Transportation Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this was all prior to the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, before the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And after Petricevic interrogated you, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Petricevic told us that he didn't know what to do with us anymore, because people were being brought constantly and that he have to take us to jail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And by jail, where -- is that where you ended up?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And which jail exactly were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It's a building adjacent to the MUP. It's a small prison which is used only for minor offences, like misdemeanour or traffic offences. Severe criminals were sent to Foca --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May we display on the screen 65 ter 3419.29.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hadzovic, I'm going to show you an image, an aerial image of Doboj. And with the help of the usher, I will ask you to mark certain locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, if that could be turned around in landscape. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The usher is going to give you a pen which will allow to you mark on the screen. Now before you make any markings, do you roughly recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the main street in Doboj, where practically all the government buildings are situated. I mean, municipal buildings

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Before the witness makes any markings, Your Honour, could we admit this image because we may use it with other witnesses as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1297. The previous exhibit admitted on page 11, line 14, of today's transcript is Exhibit P1296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, could you indicate to us the MUP building where you met Mr. Petricevic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: This is the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you told us that you were brought into a van and you were unloaded. Where exactly were you unloaded?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you mark with the letter A the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I put the letter A on both buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Are these both MUP buildings?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the location where you were unloaded, could you mark that with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you indicate to us with a letter C the prison where you were taken.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this, you told us, is the Doboj central prison.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you indicate to us where is the entrance of the prison or the door where you were brought inside the prison. Maybe you can do a little line below and put the letter D.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And facing the prison, there's another building there. Which building is that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: That's the building of the SDK, or a bank. That's the public accounting and auditing building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And to the left of the prison, there are a number of buildings. Could you indicate to us the building that is adjacent to the prison, what that is.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: This is the court-house, both the district and the municipal court. And this is the head office of a construction company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where you marked a little dot for the court, could you put the letter E.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just behind the court, do you know what that building is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Unless it has been built later on. This is a boarding house. These are residential buildings, but as for this particular building, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could seize those markings, please. And I would ask that document to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were taken inside the prison, could you tell us where you were taken to first.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: We first entered through a big metal door, maybe three doors in width, and it has another small door in it. We first came into a hall. We saw that there was an a receptionist there. And then we were taken here. We went out, and then we re-entered the building from the backyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when -- when you say we entered, this -- because you were in the courtyard. Is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: No. It's a hall. When you enter, it's a large area, a hall, a corridor, that is also separated by an identical door, three metres wide and a small door inside that can be used for coming in and going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now when you go back in, did there come a time where you faced an officer from the prison?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: A man in the uniform of a prison guard was sitting there. It's a light blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened then.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. All he did was allegedly registered us and escorted us to a cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, did you see him write anything?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. But I don't know what it is that he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now you say that you were brought to cell number 7 and you were detained with other prisoners. And I would like to ask you about these detainees. The first name you mentioned in your statement is Mr. Ilija Tipura. Could you tell the Court who Mr. Tipura was --

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- and what was his profession before the war.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Ilija Tipura was one of the most respected and prominent people in Doboj. First he was the director of the railway company. After that he was the mayor, or the president of the municipality. Since he had a Ph.D. in economics, he used to teach at the faculty in Brcko as a professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to him during the war?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He hasn't been found yet. He is still missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The next person you mentioned is Mr. Karlo Grgic. I will ask you the same question: Who was he and what was his profession?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Croat. He was commander of the police station before the war, and then he retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You indicate in your statement that on the -- I believe it was approximately the 9th of May, he taken out and told to say good-bye to his cellmates.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I have never seen him or heard of him again. Is he still missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know if, after the 9th of May, whether he was brought back to the prison?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, because, at that time, I was already in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You also mention Jusuf Sarajlic. Could you tell us what was his profession?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Bosniak. He was the manager of all shopping malls in Doboj. And for a period of time he was a member of the executive council of the Municipal Assembly of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 18, 25, I believe the witness says, "I was already in the camp," not "he." Because it might refer to the other person. Maybe you can clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, I asked you -- it's just a question of the transcript. I asked you if you knew after the 9th of May, whether Mr. Grgic was brought back. Could you repeat your answer because there is a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Because I wasn't in Doboj at the time. I was in a different camp. I, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Does that clarify it sufficiently? Yeah. Your Honour, at this time I would like to show the witness a register from the Doboj prison which was shown to him two weeks ago when he met our investigator. Now we have a version that he marked when he was met two weeks ago, but we also have an unmarked version. On the version that he was shown, he marked individuals that he knew in Doboj. It would save time to just get the documents in without having the witness to mark them again. Unless there's an objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in principle, I do not object. But the problem is that when I read the -- the witness's statement and the -- the investigator's report, it appears that some of it was -- was circled in red. When we got the copy, of course, we cannot see which -- which ones are in red and which are not. Therefore, some indication on that might be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me just verify with Mr. Smith. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand that the e-mail that was sent to you could only produce it in black and white, but the version that was in e-court was in red with an X through each name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I withdraw, because I didn't check the e-court version. Thank you very much. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In this case, could we -- this is the marked version of 65 ter 3075. However, the 65 ter number for the marked version is 10344. If we can pull that up version. 45, sorry. 10345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, what are you seeking to exhibit? Both the marked and unmarked versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will not seek to exhibit them at this moment because we will have a witness who can authenticate these records. I just want to show him the document and confirm that these are the names that he marked for Your Honours. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document? Was it shown to you a couple of weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we go to the third page, please, which has the ERN 0675-4595. I assume everybody can see the colours at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, the names that we see here which were encircled in red and have a cross through them, are these the names that you recognised at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify to the Court, are these individuals that you knew from Doboj?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see all these people at the prison, or you just knew them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I only knew them. I only knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And those that you have mentioned to us in your prison cell, those are the ones that you knew were detained?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will not go through all the pages in this document. But if you look at, for example, the first page for now, could you tell us the ethnicity of the individuals on this page?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: They are all either Bosniaks or Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Again, we see additional markings. Now you went through the entire book. And unless there's an objection from the Defence, would you say that your answer to the previous question reflects the ethnic background of all the people listed in this document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's probably my mistake. I'll rephrase. You told us on the first page that the individuals on that page were Bosniaks and Croats.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you have seen the documents two weeks ago. Can you say whether the rest of the document includes strictly Croat and Bosniak names.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Exclusively them. Both Croats and Muslims feature in all the lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I only seek to mark the document for identification. We will have a witness who be able to authenticate the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1299, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, you told us that were detained in the prison for three days and that you were released around approximately the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you told us that you were released between the hours of 8.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us why these hours are relevant?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: You know that after Doboj had been captured curfew was introduced, allowing the Muslims and Croats to move only for three hours between 8.00 a.m. and 11.00 a.m., to allow them to go shopping for food and other staples. After that time, one was not allowed to leave their residential premises. That is what was known as the curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How did you come to learn about the existence of the curfew?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: That was announced on the radio as well, in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did the radio announcement describe who took the decision to impose the curfew?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on page 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, curfew in Doboj is an adjudicated fact. I tell you which one. 1268.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So Let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just trying to clarify how he came to learn about it and who was issuing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, on page 6 of your statement you told us that you were arrested a second time on the 12th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you were first taken to a warehouse in Usora.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: There had been a raid against the entire remaining population. They loaded us onto buses and took us to Usora which is a military depot where they repaired their trucks, and there were also hangars where they kept their spare parts for cars and vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you know who was in charge at the Usora warehouse?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It was a military installation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did the installation have a commander?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: When I was brought there, there were two or three hangars there, into which we were placed, and every hangar had its own commander. The commander of my hangar was Zlatan Krekic [realtime transcript read in error "Latan Rekic"], a reserve policeman. And there were also reserve army troops who were wearing olive green grey uniforms. And they were there guarding us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The transcript at page 24, line 6, records the name Latan Rekic. Could you clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Krekic is the last name, beginning with a K.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display on the screen 65 ter 2397.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The first name is Zlatan, with a Z, not Latan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, do you see the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You saw this document for the first time yesterday, did you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could we go to page 3 of this document in B/C/S. The English version doesn't have the names, only the headers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you look at number 74.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Zlatan Krekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody else on this page?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Stanko Sljuka, Nenad Sitnicic. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on this page, do you recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Sljuka. Slobodan Pekic -- Sorry, Tekic, with a T. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know them from Doboj, from the civilian life.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: These were citizens from the town of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage, this being a payroll from the Doboj CSB, I only seek to mark it for identification. We will have a witness to authenticate it later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1300 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, You mentioned in your statement, and this is for reference at page 7, that you were transferred to Percin's Disco on the 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From the 12th until the 19th I was in those military hangars, and then we were separated. Half of the people were brought back to Doboj, probably to prison, and the rest of us were taken to this Percin discotheque.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were interrogated in the Percin's Disco?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: One day - I don't know exactly when - inspectors came from the MUP. And since the weather was nice, they put up tables outside, sat around there. There were about ten of them. And then they took us out in groups of ten or so, and each of us was interrogated by an inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you remember who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I was interrogated by a man I had been to school with, Branislav Petricevic. I mentioned him already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you recognise other inspectors?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Among others, I recognised Slobodan Dujkovic, Milan Savic. I can't remember anyone else. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was Slobodan Dujkovic interrogating other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was there anything that had happened during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He must have known this prisoner from before, and when he was interrogated him, Dujkovic took this tool for putting out fire from a nearby destroyed petrol station and hit the man on the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What happened to this man?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: So after this man was hit on the head by a shovel, he was taken back to the camp. I think he eventually got out of the camp, but I'm not sure. Because after the human shield was used, I was taken out of the camp and he stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the name of this detainee?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Cicak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was there another member of his family detained at the Percin's Disco?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: His father was there, Stipo Cicak. He was detained with the rest of us at the disco, a man of about 70-plus. He was an economist who had worked as a clerk -- as an employee at the railway company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court what happened to Mr. Stipo Cicak?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Stipo Cicak was brought from his apartment already beaten up. He was barely breathing. He was unable to drink water, and he died. Three or four days after his death, we asked them to take the body away because it was beginning to smell, and only then did the police come with a coffin and took him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You mentioned the human shields incident on 12th of July, where you were taken with 50 other detainees. Could you describe, first of all, who took you out of the disco.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th July, around 6.30, an attack began. The BH army was probably launching an attack on Doboj, although we didn't know exactly what was happening because we were locked up inside. There was a commotion in Doboj. Buses came, bringing reservist and soldiers were who supposed to up the defence against the BH army. And when things came to a head, and it looked like Doboj was about to fall, a man whose name we didn't know, we knew him only as Golub, came in, and 50 of us were taken out without any roll-call. The first 50 who were closest to the door were pushed out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: We were taken to a school building nearby. We were stripped to the waist and lined up in rows of ten. They seemed to be waiting for something. And in this waiting, one member of the MUP who used to be a chief in the MUP in the past talked to someone on the Motorola and said that Andrija Bjelosevic had approved a human shield to be used and that the human shields should be treated humanely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, how did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was standing right next to us. Because the man who had brought us out was standing facing us on -- on the other side of this column of people, and this other man shouted across the column of people to him that the human shields had been approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Who was Andrija Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: He was the chief of the CSB, the Security Services Centre, or perhaps the DB, the state security. I don't really know much about these various services in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And immediately after this Motorola call, what happened?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Then the man known as Golub immediately shot one of the men in the back of the head, Drago Kalem from Kalenovci village, and he said it was an example. If we tried to escape, we would all get a bullet in the back of the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I wish to show you a couple of documents, and that will be my examination-in-chief. First of all, could we display 65 ter 3522.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, this is a list from the CSB Doboj crime department. Could you tell us if you recognise any of the names here

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I know them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You mentioned Branislav Petricevic. Is he featured on this list?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is there anybody else on this list that you saw during these events in May or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Dujkovic. Not the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would ask again this document to be marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1301, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display 65 ter 3164.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is map of Doboj that I showed you yesterday. It will be coming up, just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, if we could zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And with the help of the usher, I will ask you to mark this map. First of all, could you indicate to us where is the main road in Doboj on this map?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Here. This road here. How shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you just put a line on it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And where are the -- first of all, where is the prison, the central prison?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It should be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you put the letter Z there.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You told us about two other locations -- well, first of all, you were taken to the Usora warehouse. If you could indicate that.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. That should be the one. Maybe this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you put the -- well, you made two dots over there. Could you put the letter U next to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we help the witness erase whatever he wants to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And finally the Percin's Disco, if you could mark that.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's not visible. It's next to the bridge, towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And from the barracks to the centre of town, what is the distance roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: About a kilometre and a half, maximum two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we seize these markings, and I would like to offer this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P13202 [sic], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I think I have a few minutes for my last topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzovic, you mentioned in your statement - and that is on the last page - that one of the two mosques in Doboj town was totally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It was destroyed -- it was first shelled by artillery and the minaret was damaged. And then they came again after the shelling, which was on the 3rd of May. They came again, and blew it up so that it was razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And where is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, adjudicated fact 1271, destruction of mosques in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: During May and June 1992, 21 Muslim and Catholic monuments in Doboj municipality including ... and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The Doboj town mosque is included in the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I have one more question, Mr. Demirdjian, for you. On your list, what is the purpose of having a document on the general list and then on the list for this witness and eventually on the list for another witness. It seems to be the same document on -- on two lists. Is there any specific purpose for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The general list was just for the purpose of having the package for all documents in relation to this municipality, and then we split the list per witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you work on the list for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a few minutes short of the break, so we may as well take the break at this point and return in 20 minutes, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, while the witness is being brought -- escorted back to the stand, could you clarify something for us, please. The -- this leak, I think was a word you used, is it -- is the search engine a government search engine which has, without authorisation, been made available to the general public? Or is this an unknown third party who has privately set up a search engine which allows access to the original government document? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand the question. I will try to the best of my knowledge to respond. Your Honour -- [Microphone not activated] can I get the witness to take off his ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Your Honour, the search engine and the database are -- authentically government. The point was that some third party without the proper authorisation put its content or a link on the web. Therefore, the -- the basic document which is -- which is the -- the government document has been somehow -- has been probably copied and put on the -- on the web. That is as far as I could found out at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But is there a document, or is there only the search engine? Because, I mean, we are probably speaking about hundreds of thousands of names in that document. So I imagine that the document doesn't exist as a physical document. It -- it exists as a database. And what you get is, through the search engine, you get access, unauthorised access, to this database. Is that the way we understand it or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, my -- that is completely correct. It is not a document. It is a database which contains the names, the dates, and the -- the relevant names of the -- of the Croatian Army units where this particular person at a certain point in time served his -- his military service, during period 1990 until 1995. This database does not contain -- that is not a document. It is a database and a search engine where you -- when you type the names, you get the response with the name and the -- or number of the names if they are the same and the dates and -- and the units which -- which are referring to that particular individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The reason we discussed it is that if we were to follow Mr. Hannis's suggestion that we should ask somehow the Croatian Ministry of Defence to -- to tell us whether the information that can be gained by using this search engine is, indeed, authentic, then the question arises - and this was what we were discussing in the break - whether we would have to limit ourselves to asking the government about the authenticity of information relating to specific persons; or, whether we could ask the government to verify -- to confirm or to -- the opposite, disconfirm, unconfirm, that the database, as such, is still original and had not been tampered with. I don't know if -- Mr. Hannis has any idea how this can be done, and who should do it, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't. But if I could raise an additional point. I now have a hard copy of some of the pages that, I guess, Mr. Zecevic has presented out from the database. And what it has is a name, a first and last name, what appears to be a name of a unit or a component that the person allegedly served with, and a date of service. But it is only a name. There's no indication of the father's name, the age of this person, the date of birth, where they're from. And as we've seen in the region, a lot of times there are similar names. There's several individuals with the same name. So there is really no way of linking that name with the name of the person this witness has talked about in a cell with. It is too tenuous, and especially given the uncertainty about where this database comes from. And if somebody is able, without authorisation, to copy it and put it on the Internet, I suggest to you, they're also probably able to manipulate the data that is in it. And it's not something that you should feel comfortable and relying on at this point without some further showing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may quickly respond. I agree with what Mr. Hannis is saying, but we are bound to -- to use the material that we received from the -- from the -- from the Office of the Prosecutor. Neither the witness provides the -- the father's name, the date of birth, the whereabouts, or any other -- or any other data of that respect. So he provides with the name. He provided us with the name and his nationality, and we tried to search the names. That is -- as simple as that. Your Honours, if I may say so, I believe the -- the -- the shortcut to this -- because we don't know at this point, Maybe we might need to access this database quite a few times in the future. Now, what I would suggest is that we will approach the Ministry or the Government of Croatia and ask if they can verify the authenticity of that specific site. If they can verify the authenticity of the -- of the data contained on that site is authentic or not, I believe would be a shortcut how to do it. Or -- or ask the -- or ask the Croatian Government to provide the whole -- the whole database, which would definitely take some more time than ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The question still remains whether it is -- it is only the access to the official database that has been hacked and made public or whether it is the database as such that has been hacked. And if it's the database as such, it can be manipulated by -- by the persons who hacked it. If it's the database and a search machine that has been put on it by the hackers, that's different when -- from the situation where it is only the -- the access, the way to axis the official search machine and the official database that would be hacked. So that's the first -- first type of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I -- I understand, Your Honours, but as my knowledge of this only comes from the public media, I am -- I have given the, I believe, the fair amount of information or basically all the information that is my possession at this point, to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, the -- returning to the -- what I understand your immediate problem or question to be in terms of your -- how you proceed with the cross-examination of this witness, it seems to us that there would no prohibition on your framing your questions, subject of course to the rules about good faith and all of that. And if, at some point, we have a to return to this question of the -- this documentary evidence, we will see where that leads us. But at this point I think can you do no more than ask the question, such questions as you consider appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I understand. Thank you very much, Your Honours. Your Honours, may I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Hadzovic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please confirm for me whether it's correct that you gave your first statement back in August 1992, on the 11th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that statement was given to the security authorities of the army, or the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: At the time it was the provisional Ministry of the Interior that had been formed in exile, in the exiled municipality of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then also to the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you gave another statement, on the 20th of July, 1995. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is it maybe Tesanj?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps it might be easier if the usher gave the witness the copies of his statements to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are looking at that statement of 20th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was in Tesanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you and I speak the same language, please, let's not overlap.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this statement of the 20th July 1995 is your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then, on the 22nd of June, 1998, before the investigating judge of the cantonal court in Zenica, Safet Hadrovic, you gave another statement.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then, on the 12th of March, 2001, you gave another statement before the IC -- for the ICTY, which is now exhibited as P1296.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then, on the 11th of November, 2001, you gave another short statement, in fact a supplemental statement, to the March 2001 statement; correct? That should be tab 6.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then, on the 30th November, 2007, to the Centre for the Investigation of War Crimes of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you gave a statement which is in fact a record of questioning of a witness?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, in April, 9 April 2010, you gave another statement to the investigators of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Also, on the 30th November and the 1st of December, you testified before this court in the Stanisic and Simatovic case.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Also, before the War Crimes Court, you testified in the Predrag Kujundzic case as a prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, P1296, you say that, after the multi-party elections in 1991, Ahmed Alicic, the SDA candidate, was appointed president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Doboj municipality.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also claim in your statement that the chief the MUP was a Muslim, called Hasan Hrnjadovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement, and I suppose you can confirm, that you remember how Alija Izetbegovic asked the Muslims to refuse mobilization call-ups into the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement that in April 1992, you were dismissed from work. That's page 3 of your statement. You can look at it. It's P1296, page 3. You say: "In April 1992, I was dismissed from work. I was working for a small enterprise with another seven colleagues."

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Hadzovic, that you were not working for an enterprise. You were working for the Association of Physical Education Organisations?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact that this organisation of physical education organisations was a municipal enterprise, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It's a regional, municipal enterprise. It provided all the services for all the physical culture organisations in the Doboj area, organisation and such. Organisation of events, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it was financed by the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also say that you were dismissed because you were a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I and a Croat female colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how is it possible that you were dismissed from an enterprise controlled by the municipality, when the president of the municipality was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the takeover the power had already taken place, the takeover by Serbs. Because they had not agreed with the referendum for the separation, and they staged a putsch. They also dismissed all the Muslims from the police force because the party appointments -- the party appointments had not been complied with, and all these people lost their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you were answering the questions of my learned friend, you said that the 3rd May was the date of, as you put it, liberation of Doboj. And you were using the term ironically.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's when Doboj was shelled. The aggression had started, and Doboj was cleansed from Muslims and Croats. But there had been preparations for that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir, that Ahmed Alicic, the president of the municipality, continued in his position until the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Whether he did not, I don't know. I know exactly when I was I was dismissed. The manager, Jovo Popovic, invited us for a meeting and told us that it had been ordered that all Muslims and Croats be dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it is clear to you that this is illogical. If the president of the municipality and the whole municipal authority is under the control of the SDA party, the Muslim national party, then how would these same authorities in the municipalities dismiss Muslims because they were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: In practice, they did not have any power in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, sir, that the commander of the JNA barracks in Doboj was Colonel Cazim Hadzic, also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, until 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about April now. If the president of the municipality was a Muslim, if the chief of the SUP was a Muslim, and the commander of the military garrison in Doboj was Muslim, then on what basis, do you claim that they had no power?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Simply because they had been placed in those positions after the elections. After that, the Serbs mutinied and refused to recognise the democratically-elected authorities in Doboj, and they took over all the power in Doboj for all practical purposes. And they --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But this takeover happened on the 3rd May, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It was all over by the 3rd of May. A certain amount of organisation was needed to take over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that parts of Doboj, such as Carsija and Tvrdjava, the fortress, populated the mainly by Muslims, were under the control of the Green Berets and the Patriotic League, already at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. There were no Green Berets in Doboj, and there was no Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you will remember, won't you, that there were nightguards, check-points in those neighbourhoods, where even the police or any other official authority had no access. And those check-points were manned by the Green Berets, armed, and members of the Patriotic League, also armed. You will remember that.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: The check-points existed at the entrance to the Carsija and the exit from Carsija, and they were manned by local citizens. They were neither Green Berets or members of any Patriotic League. Those were self-organised citizens who stood guard against a possible attack, because, by that time, there had already appeared in town reservists and all kinds of armed men with cockades and similar emblems, and Muslims were afraid of being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt you, but my time is limited. You said all of that in your statement. Just give me more concise answers, please. So, at these entry and exit check-points in Carsija that were manned by the local residents, were those local residents armed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had shotguns and pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Isn't it true that on the 3rd of May, the commander, Cazim Hadzic, the Doboj garrison commander, issued an order for those paramilitary units, the Green Berets and the Patriotic League, and he called them paramilitary units, to submit and surrender those illegally possessed weapons?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. All I know --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You don't know. Isn't it true, and do you remember that on that particular day, an ultimatum was issued pursuant to Cazim Hadzic's order, a Muslim colonel, for the JNA [as interpreted] to surrender weapons on the 3rd of May by 1800 hours?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of May, 1992, Slobodan Karagic drove through Doboj, a member of the SDS and he had a megaphone. I don't know whose orders he followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will surely remember that during that afternoon an armed clash occurred which was the motive for the JNA for opening --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Preparing and targeting certain locations in Tvrdjava and Carsija as military targets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were only guards in Carsija. This ultimatum was to surrender weapons until 1600 hours. It was announced through the megaphone. And then without any notification, artillery fire was opened on Dramija [phoen], Gradina, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were in Doboj on that day, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you hadn't heard that there was an armed conflict that preceded artillery fire of certain targets in Carsija and Tvrdjava?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: No I hadn't, even though I lived in Carsija. All I heard was the artillery fire coming from the tanks and targeting the mosque. Later on, there was shooting. There was exchange of fire, but I don't know who was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Hadzic [sic] --

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Hadzovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Hadzovic. I have a problem trying to establish exactly or, at least, approximately the dates, because in your statements you have provided different information, which is probably understandable after such a long time. Therefore, I will try to recap this, and we shall try to establish the real situation. The fact is that you were taken for the first time to the MUP building on the 6th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you were interviewed by Branislav Petricevic. You spoke about that on page 14, lines 6 to 8. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in the course of that interview, I suppose that he asked you whether you had some illegal weapons, rifle, an automatic rifle, or something of the sort; whether you were a member of the Green Berets, the Patriotic League, or any other military formation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: No. Petri and I - I mean Branislav Petricevic - knew each other very well. And he knew very well that I hadn't taken part or belonged to either Green Berets or the Patriotic League or any formation. He knew I had a licenced weapon issued to me within my duties, because I was a cashier, and this was issued to me by MUP. There was no record made. All he told to me was, They keep bringing people in, and we don't know what to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that on that day you returned home after 5.00?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you went there for the first time on the 6th -- on the 3rd -- or, rather, 6th May. You had this interview with Branislav Petricevic, and you returned home sometime in the afternoon of the 6th of May, after 5.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that, soldiers with -- with red berets, brought you in or arrested you, let's say, on the 8th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of May, you were taken to the prison that you described today.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You spent three days in prison.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: It was three days and two nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you were released within the legal term, which is 72 hours; that is to say, on the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then, on the 12th of June, once again, the soldiers with red berets arrested you again, along with your brother.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, the second time around, on the 8th of May, when you were arrested, did Branislav Petricevic tell you then that your brother was already in cell number 7?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that second time around, on the 8th of May, you also talked to Branislav Petricevic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He seemed to be the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So your brother was already in prison on the 8th, and he was released, together with you, on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then, on the 12th of June, both of you together were arrested by these soldiers with the red berets.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: Can I explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
utterances.text: My brother has an apartment in a different part of town. In the month of May, since his family was not with him - they were away - he came to stay with me. I lived in our joint family house, and my 14-year-old child was there also. We were staying there together. Now when this general purge of Carsija neighbourhood began, we were both rounded up, and the minor child remained at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But after that, your son went to stay with some relatives, if I remember one of your statements well.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HADZOVIC
